LLM Optimization Checklist for Content and Marketing

By lowob · 11 March 2026 · Updated 10 November 2026 · 4-minute read · Distribution / AI search

If customers ask AI assistants about your category, your site should be easy to find, accurate, accessible and worth citing. This checklist focuses on those fundamentals, without promising a guaranteed shortcut into AI answers.

The previous article explained how AI assistants choose what to cite. This one is the list of things to do about it. None of it is exotic; most of it is the discipline good content always required, applied with a machine reader in mind.

Write pages that answer one question

Each important page should exist to answer a question a buyer actually asks, and should answer it in the first paragraph. Put the question, or a close paraphrase, in the page title and the first heading. State the answer plainly, then explain. A reader should be able to find the central answer quickly, without needing to wade through several paragraphs of marketing language.

Audit the current site for pages that do this. Most companies find that their highest-traffic pages describe the company and their most useful pages are buried three clicks down.

Make claims that can be checked

Replace "leading," "innovative," and "trusted" with facts: what the product does, for whom, at what cost, since when, with what result. Give definitions where the category is new. Give numbers where they can be substantiated, and date them. Comparisons with named criteria can be useful because they answer practical buyer questions.

Structure for machines without writing for them

Clear heading hierarchy. Short sections. Lists and tables where the content is naturally a list or a table. Descriptive link text. A summary or definition block near the top of long pages. Content rendered in HTML rather than assembled by scripts after the page loads, so it is readable by crawlers that do not execute JavaScript.

Use accurate structured data where it supports standard search features. Google says no special AI markup is required.

Earn independent references without manufacturing consensus

Accurate directory entries, partner documentation and legitimate reporting can help customers discover or verify a company. Aim to be covered because there is something worth saying, not to repeat identical claims in places you control.

Google explicitly cautions against inauthentic mentions and AI-search gimmicks. A citation from an assistant is not guaranteed by the number of brand mentions or backlinks.

Answer the questions people ask assistants

Ask the assistants directly: what do they say about your category, your competitors, and you? Which sources do they cite? What questions do they think a buyer would ask next? Those questions, and the sources currently winning them, are the content plan.

Then write the definitive answer to each, publish it on a page built to be extracted, and make sure at least two third-party sources say something consistent.

Keep the technical basics honest

Use stable canonical URLs, crawlable text, clear navigation, a clean sitemap and accurate structured data where it serves normal search needs. Google says there is no special schema or llms.txt requirement for its AI features.

Review crawler rules deliberately. OpenAI distinguishes OAI-SearchBot, for search, from GPTBot, for training. Blocking one does not automatically block the other. Different assistants use different indexing arrangements, and crawler permission alone does not guarantee inclusion.

Measure it

Traditional analytics will show referrals from AI assistants where they pass a referrer, and branded search volume as a proxy for recall. Beyond that, the practical measure is manual: a monthly set of the twenty questions that matter most to the business, asked of the major assistants, with the answers and citations recorded. Watch whether the company appears, whether it is described accurately, and which sources are cited instead.

That is not sophisticated. It is enough to know whether the work is landing, which is more than most companies know today.

lowob takeaways

  • Publish direct, independently checkable answers to real buyer questions.
  • Use crawlable pages, accurate metadata, coherent internal links and genuine references.
  • Measure visibility by assistant and question; distinguish search crawling from model training.

Sources and notes

Google Search Central, AI Features and Your Website. Google says standard SEO practices remain relevant.

Google Search Central, Guide to Optimizing for Generative AI Features. No special schema, llms.txt file or content chunking is required for Google AI search.

OpenAI, Overview of Crawlers. OAI-SearchBot governs search appearance separately from GPTBot training crawling.
